newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT - CCB FIRST-HALF 1996 EARNINGS STATEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - CCB FIRST-HALF 1996 EARNINGS STATEMENT.

text.p: Following is the full text of the first-half 1996 earnings statement of Belgian publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB).
CREDIT COMMUNAL HALF-YEARLY RESULTS 1996
EMBARGO UNTILL 11.09.96 - 2 P.M.
CONSOLIDATED RESULTS
Balance sheet data

On 30 June 1996 the consolidated balance sheet total of Credit Communal amounted to BEF 3,727 billion, an increase of BEF 395 billion or 11.8% compared to June 1995. All subsidiaries contributed to this increase.

In the meantime, the group has been constantly expanding. With a share of 94.8% in the consolidated balance sheet total, the parent company and the BIL group remain the major spearheads of the Credit Communal group. Banque Internationale a Luxembourg, of which Credit Communal is the reference shareholder with 52%, represents 24.7%. Investment advice companies were included in the consolidation for the first time. Equity method accounting was applied to BBL.

At the end of June 1996, the financial means of the Credit Communal group amounted to BEF 3,450 billion, an increase of BEF 357 billion or 11.5% in comparison with the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

The consolidated deposits of the credit institutions rose by 51.4% to BEF 785 billion. The financial means entrusted by customers to the Credit Communal group went up by BEF 90 billion or 3.5% to BEF 2,665 billion on 30 June 1996. In this regard, the increase in deposits was slightly smaller (+ 3.3%) than in savings bonds and debentures (+ 3.8%).

Whereas sight deposits and savings deposits grew considerably (+ BEF 46 billion or + 16% and + BEF 59 billion or + 23% respectively), investors' interest in fixed-term deposits diminished (- BEF 62 billion or - 8%). The rise in savings bonds and debentures can be attributed almost exclusively to the subsidiaries, which implemented a number of important issue programmes for certificates and debenture loans. As far as the parent company is concerned, the outstanding amount of savings bonds and debentures decreased.

On the assets side, loans and advances to credit institutions rose from BEF 600 billion in June 1995 to BEF 818 billion at the end of June 1996. This rise of 36.2% is considerably lower than the increase in the corresponding item on the liabilities side. Just like last year, the group remained a net investor on the interbank market. However, the amount fell from BEF 82 billion on 30 June 1995 to BEF 33 billion on 30 June 1996.

During the same period, outstanding credits to customers increased by 4.7%. At the end of June 1996, outstanding loans and advances to customers amounted on a consolidated basis to BEF 1,460 billion as against BEF 1,394 billion one year earlier. Outstanding credits to public customers went up by 2.6%. The increase in credits to private customers, enterprises and self-employed persons amounted to 9.3%.
Financial investments rose by 7% to BEF 1,277 billion on 30 June 1996. Treasury bills and debentures of public issuers constitute almost three-quarters (72%) of the securities in portfolio.

Equity capital of the group went up by BEF 10 billion (+ 15.8%) to BEF 74 billion. Subordinated debt was raised by 8 billion to BEF 52.5 billion. At the end of June 1996, equity plus subordinated loans add up to BEF 126 billion as against BEF 108 billion one year earlier, an increase of 17.1%.
Income statement
Interest profit went up by BEF 1 billion (or 5.1%) to BEF 20.7 billion between June 1995 and June 1996. Both interest payable and interest receivable decreased as a result of lower interest rates.

Various banking profits showed a sharp rise, up by 30.9% (+ BEF 2.6 billion). At the end of June 1996 they amounted to BEF 11.1 billion, increasing their share in the total operating profit to 35%. This substantial increase was due to a growth in profits on financial transactions and in profits from financial services.
At the end of June 1996, the total operating revenue amounted to BEF 31.8 billion, compared to BEF 28.2 billion one year earlier (+ BEF 3.6 billion or + 12.9%).

During the period under review, general charges showed a limited rise of 4.7%. The gross operating income went up from BEF 11.4 billion at the end of June 1995 to BEF 14.2 billion at the end of June 1996, an increase of nearly BEF 3 billion or 25%.
At the end of June 1996 depreciations, write-downs and provisions totalled BEF 5.3 billion, i.e. 0.3 billion less than one year earlier.

After deduction of taxes in the amount of BEF 3.7 billion (a 69% increase) and taking into account the equity accounted enterprises, the consolidated half-yearly net profit came to BEF 6.2 billion. In comparison with the same period in 1995 this represents an increase of BEF 1.8 billion or 39.7%.
The share of the group in this consolidated result amounted to BEF 5.4 billion, i. e. 41.3% more than last year.
RESULTS ON A COMPANY BASIS
The results of the parent company show the same tendency as those of the group:
- the balance sheet total increased by 10% to BEF 2,756 billion at the end of June;

- customer assets showed an increase of 1.6% to BEF 1,970 billion. The outstanding amount on regulated savings accounts rose by 22.7% to BEF 317 billion. Fixed-term accounts showed a more limited rise. The outstanding amount of savings bonds and debentures dropped by 3.2%; - loans and advances to customers went up by 7% and totalled BEF 1,306 billion at the end of June;
- financial investments showed a slight drop (- 2.5%) and amounted to BEF 895 billion at the end of June;
- net profits added up to BEF 4.3 billion in the first half of the year, a growth of 44.7% compared to the same period of last year.
EXCELLENT RATIOS
Due to the favourable results of Credit Communal and its subsidiaries, the bank amply complies with the national and international profitability and solvency standards, the main of which are:
- the return on equity (ROE), i. e. 15.1% for the group and 12.3% for the parent company;
- the risk assets ratio, calculated according to the new Capital Adequacy Directive, i. e. 13.20% for the group and 12.68% on a company basis.
